name: Pansy Ho
current_role: Group Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Shun Tak Holdings; co-chairperson, MGM China Holdings
profile: Daughter of the late Macau gaming magnate Stanley Ho, Pansy Ho runs Shun Tak Holdings (property, hotels and the Hong Kong-Macau TurboJET ferries) and holds stakes in MGM China and SJM Holdings. She made more than $1.5bn from MGM China's 2011 IPO and is now a prominent global tourism advocate, serving as a UN Tourism Ambassador.
interesting_fact: She dabbled in Hong Kong show business as an actress in the 1980s and helped promote her sister Josie Ho's acting and singing career.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 she founded the Global Tourism Economy Research Centre, which organises the annual Global Tourism Economy Forum in Macau; she was named a UNWTO Tourism Ambassador in 2018 and became the first official PATA Foundation Ambassador.
notes: Shun Tak has issued a statement warning about false AI-generated content about the group online, so check sources carefully. Her sister Maisy Ho, an executive director, died in April 2026; avoid that topic. Tourism (GTEF, UN Tourism) is the most natural hook. Shun Tak's site blocked scraping, so no email was verified.

name: Maria Del Pino Y Calvo Soleto
current_role: Non-Executive Director of Ferrovial N.V. and President of the Fundación Rafael del Pino
profile: María del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo is the eldest child of Ferrovial founder Rafael del Pino y Moreno (d. 2008) and holds about 8.7% of Ferrovial through her company Menosmares, S.L. She has sat on Ferrovial's board since 2006; her brother Rafael is executive chairman. Since 2000 she has also led the family's Fundación Rafael del Pino.
interesting_fact: Her father personally named her president of the Fundación Rafael del Pino when he created it in 2000. Its mission is to train future leaders, and it has since funded hundreds of 'Becas de Excelencia' scholarships for Spanish graduates.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business she interned at the European Commission in Brussels, worked in the International Relations Secretariat of Spain's UCD party from 1979, and later volunteered with the development NGO Codespa until 2000. She studied economics at Universidad Complutense and holds an IESE PDD.
notes: The input spells her name 'Calvo Soleto'; the correct spelling is Calvo-Sotelo. She is very private and has reportedly given only one interview. The best route is through the Fundación Rafael del Pino (general info email), which runs economics and energy-policy events. She also sits on the Princess of Asturias Foundation's board of trustees.

name: Brenninkmeijer family
current_role: Family owners of COFRA Holding AG (Zug, Switzerland), parent of C&A, Bregal Investments and Sunrock; chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, with Florian Brenninkmeyer due to take over in April 2027
profile: This Dutch-German dynasty founded the C&A clothing chain in 1841 and owns it through the Swiss holding company COFRA, alongside private equity (Bregal), real estate and renewable energy investments. Around 2026 the group reported roughly €40bn under management and was handing control to the sixth generation, with Georg Wunderlin as its first non-family CEO.
interesting_fact: C&A takes its name from the initials of the founding brothers Clemens and August Brenninkmeyer, who opened their first textile shop in Sneek, Netherlands, in 1841. Six generations later the business is still entirely family-owned.
deep_cut_fact: Long before ESG became fashionable, Marcel Brenninkmeijer founded Good Energies in 2001 to run COFRA's renewables portfolio. It backed wind and solar developers and the Atlantic Wind Connection offshore transmission backbone, a strong energy hook.
notes: This is a family (hundreds of members), not an individual, and it is famously private. For an energy podcast, the best individual targets are probably COFRA chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, incoming chair Florian Brenninkmeyer, or the Sunrock solar business. Contact is through the COFRA newsroom; no email could be scraped. The family won the 2026 Kellogg Family Leadership Award.

name: Gabriele Volkmann
current_role: Shareholder (heir) in Brose Fahrzeugteile SE & Co. KG, Coburg; no public operating role found
profile: According to Forbes (2018), Gabriele Volkmann is an heir to Brose, the family-owned German auto-parts supplier founded by her great-grandfather Max Brose and built into a global player by her uncle Michael Stoschek. Brose is split between the Stoschek and Volkmann family lines; her mother Christine Volkmann is a shareholder.
interesting_fact: Brose makes mechatronic parts such as window regulators, seat adjusters, door systems and e-bike motors, components that are 'largely invisible to drivers' yet fitted to cars worldwide. It is among the largest family-owned automotive suppliers.
notes: Very private; she appeared on Forbes only in 2018, and almost nothing is published about her personally. German press says the shareholders include Christine Volkmann 'and her eldest daughter', which may be her, but this is unconfirmed. Brose is chaired by Maximilian Stoschek, and he or the Brose press office is the realistic route. Brose's site has no scrapeable press email.

name: Madhukar Parekh
profile: Madhukar Parekh, a chemical engineer, joined Pidilite, the adhesives company founded by his father Balvant Parekh in 1959, in 1971. He built it into India's dominant adhesives, sealants and construction-chemicals maker, best known for Fevicol and M-seal. He remains chairman, with Bharat Puri as MD; brother Ajay Parekh and family members also hold board seats.
interesting_fact: Pidilite's Fevicol is one of India's most iconic brands, built over decades through famously witty advertising. Pidilite's 2025-26 annual report pays tribute to the late ad legend Piyush Pandey, whose work helped shape the brand.
deep_cut_fact: He placed 4th in India's IIT JEE entrance exam but chose to study chemical engineering at Bombay's UDCT instead. He then earned an M.S. in chemical engineering at the University of Wisconsin (1969) and worked at Abbott Laboratories in the US before joining the family firm in 1971.
notes: Low public profile; he rarely gives interviews. Corporate communications or IR is the route. The JEE rank detail comes from Wikipedia citing Forbes India (2014); it is worth confirming against the original Forbes India article before using it.

name: Senapathy Gopalakrishnan
current_role: Chairman, Axilor Ventures (Bengaluru seed fund and accelerator); co-founder of Infosys
profile: Kris Gopalakrishnan co-founded Infosys in 1981 and served as its CEO and MD (2007-11) and vice chairman (2011-14). Since retiring he has chaired Axilor Ventures, which backs early-stage and deep-tech startups. He is one of India's biggest funders of brain research, at IISc and IIT Madras, and a frequent voice on AI and 'Unicorn 2.0' deep tech.
interesting_fact: He gave Rs 225 crore to set up IISc's Centre for Brain Research, the largest gift the institute had ever received from an individual. He also funded IIT Madras's Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre, which maps human brains at cellular resolution.
deep_cut_fact: Data-policy hook: he chaired the Indian government's (MeitY) expert committee on a Non-Personal Data Governance Framework and was the first chairperson of the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub. Trained as a physicist (M.Sc. Physics, IIT Madras, 1977), he began as a software engineer at Patni Computer Systems in 1979.
notes: Very accessible and a frequent speaker at CII, startup and AI events. He talks openly about AI's impact on IT services, so he is a strong fit for a data and AI podcast. Best route is through Axilor or CII; Itihaasa (itihaasa.com) is his IT-history project.

name: Jason Murray
current_role: Co-Founder, CEO and Chairman, PACS Group, Inc. (NYSE: PACS)
profile: Jason Murray, a licensed nursing home administrator and former healthcare executive, co-founded PACS Group with Mark Hancock in 2013. Starting with two skilled nursing facilities, it has grown into a Utah-based post-acute care platform with about 387 facilities in 17 states. PACS listed on the NYSE in 2024; Murray owns roughly a third of the shares and still runs the company.
interesting_fact: PACS went from two skilled-nursing facilities in 2013 to a national post-acute care platform with nearly 400 facilities in about a decade, then listed on the NYSE in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He was named Ernst & Young's 2023 Mountain West Entrepreneur of the Year and was a finalist for EY's national award that year. He is a Fellow of the American College of Healthcare Executives (FACHE) and says he enjoys 'anything related to sports and athletics'.
notes: Route through Brooks Stevenson (corporate communications). PACS has faced short-seller and accounting scrutiny since 2024, so keep outreach focused on entrepreneurship and scaling. The web-search budget ran out at this point; facts come from the PACS IR site.

name: Robert Edward (Ted) Turner
profile: CNN founder and media pioneer Ted Turner died on 6 May 2026, aged 87.
notes: Deceased (6 May 2026), per CNN and AP obituaries cited on Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Turner). Not an outreach target. His legacy organisations (Turner Enterprises, Turner Foundation, UN Foundation, Nuclear Threat Initiative) continue.

name: Martin
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Bouygues SA (CEO role passed to Olivier Roussat in 2021)
profile: Martin Bouygues, son of founder Francis Bouygues, ran the French construction, telecoms and media group Bouygues as chairman and CEO from 1989 to 2021 and remains chairman. With his brother Olivier he controls the family's stake through SCDM. The group spans Bouygues Construction, Colas, Equans (energy services), Bouygues Telecom and TF1.
interesting_fact: With his brother Olivier he owns Bordeaux's Château Montrose (a Saint-Estèphe second growth), Château Tronquoy-Lalande and the Loire's Clos Rougeard. Since 2018 he has also owned Burgundy's Domaine Henri Rebourseau.
deep_cut_fact: His only diploma is the baccalauréat. He joined Bouygues in 1974 as a site works supervisor (conducteur de travaux), worked on the Forum des Halles site in Paris, and founded catalogue home-builder Maison Bouygues in 1978. In 1989, at 37, he became the youngest CEO in the CAC 40.
notes: The input entry 'Martin' (Hurun, shared with Olivier Bouygues, source Bouygues) is Martin Bouygues, born 1952. Energy and data-centre angle: Equans and Bouygues Energies & Services do energy and data-centre infrastructure. Bouygues.com blocked automated access, so no press email was captured; use the group's press page. He is also Commander of the Ordre national du Mérite (2021).

name: Sandeep Pravinbhai Engineer
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Astral Limited (Ahmedabad)
profile: Sandeep Engineer is a first-generation entrepreneur and chemical engineer. He spent eight years in pharmaceutical bulk drugs before founding Astral Poly Technik in 1996, now Astral Ltd, a leading Indian maker of plastic pipes and building materials. He has since expanded into adhesives (Resinova, 2014), water tanks (Sarita, 2020) and paints (Gem Paints).
interesting_fact: In 1998 Astral launched CPVC piping in India for the first time. Plastic pipes were then barely accepted against metal, so Engineer spent years educating plumbers and builders to create the category Astral now leads.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a project engineer at a pharmaceuticals company, then became a distributor and later manufactured pharmaceutical remedies. He said he had been fascinated by polymers since his graduation days, which led to the pivot into piping. He also completed Harvard Business School's OPM programme.
notes: Self-made founder story with a strong entrepreneurship angle. His wife Jagruti Engineer is a whole-time director. Contact is through Astral corporate (info@) or company secretary or IR via the investors page.

name: Sybill Storz
profile: Dr. h.c. mult. Sybill Storz, longtime head and later chair of endoscopy maker KARL STORZ, died at 88, as announced by the company on 1 Dec 2025 (she died the preceding Friday).
notes: Deceased (late Nov 2025) per the KARL STORZ obituary press release. Her son Karl-Christian Storz has been sole managing director since 2019, and press@karlstorz.com is the company press contact if the family or company is of interest.

name: Richard Sands
current_role: Non-management Director, Constellation Brands (NYSE: STZ); former CEO (1993-2007) and chairman (1999-2018)
profile: Richard Sands joined his father Marvin's Canandaigua Wine Company in 1979 and, with his brother Rob, turned it through serial acquisitions into Constellation Brands. The ~$10bn-revenue group owns Robert Mondavi and holds the US rights to Corona and Modelo. He was CEO from 1993 to 2007 and chairman until 2018, and he still sits on the board. He lives in Canandaigua, New York.
interesting_fact: Under the Sands brothers, Constellation invested about $4bn in cannabis producer Canopy Growth in 2018, one of the largest bets by a mainstream drinks company on legal cannabis.
deep_cut_fact: He once worked as a delivery driver during a break from college (Forbes). He is also an RIT trustee: he and his wife Jennifer gave money for the Sands Family Studios in RIT's School for American Crafts, dedicated in 2011 as part of a $2m renovation.
notes: Confirmed on the board via the Constellation IR governance page (2026). The IR contact is corporate, not personal. In 2016 the Sands family gave $61m to the Rochester Area Community Foundation, its largest gift ever.

name: Qi Zhenbo
current_role: Founder of Meione (美ONE / 美腕, Shanghai), per Hurun listings
profile: Hurun lists Qi Zhenbo (戚振波) as the founder of Meione, a Shanghai 'new retail' unicorn. Meione (美ONE) is the agency behind top livestream seller Li Jiaqi: it signed him in late 2016 after he won a L'Oréal-sponsored Taobao livestreaming contest, and it runs his livestream e-commerce business.
interesting_fact: 美ONE ran the late-2016 L'Oréal 'BA网红化' Taobao Live contest that discovered Li Jiaqi, who arrived in Shanghai with RMB 2,000 and became China's 'Lipstick King' of livestream selling.
notes: Low-profile founder. Identity rests on the Hurun listing (戚振波 / Meione); I could not independently confirm his biography because the web-search budget was exhausted and Baidu Baike blocked access. Treat this as a lead. The best route is probably through 美腕/美ONE corporate PR.

name: Daniel Rocher
current_role: Major family shareholder of Groupe Rocher; founder of Daniel Jouvance (marine cosmetics)
profile: Daniel Rocher, son of Yves Rocher (founder of Groupe Rocher, 1959), founded the marine-ingredient skincare brand Daniel Jouvance in 1980; it later became part of the group. With his nephew Bris Rocher he is one of the largest shareholders of the family-controlled group (Yves Rocher, Arbonne, Dr Pierre Ricaud, Petit Bateau; about €2.4bn in sales). Forbes lists him as living in Rennes.
interesting_fact: He is a sculptor and art collector. In 2019 he bought a castle in Provence and turned it into an open-air sculpture gallery.
notes: Private; no personal channels found. The art and sculpture angle (the Provence castle gallery) is the best personal hook, but I could not find the castle's name or website because the web-search budget was exhausted. The Daniel Jouvance site blocked automated access.

name: Michael Ying
current_role: Former chairman of Esprit Holdings; philanthropist (Yan Ai Foundation)
profile: Michael Ying Lee Yuen, born 1949 in Hong Kong, built the Asian sourcing and distribution arm of Esprit and helped turn it into a global brand, serving as chairman until 2006. He sold most of his stake over the following years; his remaining shares passed to his daughters, who sold them in 2021. He keeps a low profile and focuses on his Yan Ai Foundation, which funds education and healthcare for poor children in mainland China.
interesting_fact: During his 13-year tenure as chairman, Esprit's sales grew 30-fold, from HK$769.7m in 1993 to HK$23.3bn in fiscal 2006 (Bloomberg data).
deep_cut_fact: His Esprit story began in the early 1970s, when he started doing business with founders Susie and Doug Tompkins (Doug also co-founded The North Face). He became their Asian sourcing agent, which grew into Esprit Far East; his family roots are in Wenchang, Hainan.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. The Yan Ai Foundation (founded 2006) is the most plausible route, but I could not verify its website because the web-search budget was exhausted. Parts of his Wikipedia early-life section are unsourced, so confirm before quoting.

name: Bent Jensen
current_role: Owner and CEO, LINAK A/S (Nordborg, Denmark), per Forbes 2026
profile: Bent Jensen, a mechanical engineer, took over his grandfather's 1907 blacksmith business, Christian Jensen & Sons, in 1976. He reinvented it around the electric linear actuator, renaming it LINAK in 1984. The family-owned company now makes actuators for hospital beds, height-adjustable desks, furniture and industrial uses, with factories in Denmark, the US, China and Slovakia.
interesting_fact: LINAK is short for 'Lineær Aktuator'. The company kept a significant share of its production in Denmark by investing heavily in automation and robotics.
deep_cut_fact: In 1979, as a newly graduated engineer, he came up with the electric linear actuator while talking with a friend from his student days who had a disability and needed a way to adjust his wheelchair. That conversation is the origin of today's LINAK.

public_contacts.value: bsp@linak.com (Birgit Spek, PA to the CEO, press and media enquiries)

notes: Strong engineer-founder story with a manufacturing and automation angle. Conveniently, the published press contact is the CEO's PA.

name: Koh Wee Meng
current_role: Founder, Executive Chairman & CEO, Fragrance Group (Singapore)
profile: Koh Wee Meng, son of a jeweller and a schoolteacher, left Aspial, his family's jewellery business, in the 1990s to start property developer Fragrance Group. Its early projects in Geylang earned him the nickname 'Geylang King'. He took Fragrance private in 2021, and it now holds property and hotels in Singapore, Australia and the UK, where it has made about a dozen hotel acquisitions since 2017.
interesting_fact: Drawing on his jewellery roots, he named his early budget hotels after precious stones: Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald and so on.
deep_cut_fact: His investing motto, quoted by Forbes, is 'Only buy and hold what you are able to afford.'
notes: Self-made and low-key in media. The only route is the corporate contact email or form. His brother Koh Wee Seng separately runs Aspial.

name: Avram Glazer
current_role: Executive Co-Chairman, Manchester United; co-owner, Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Chairman of the Board, INNOVATE Corp. (NYSE: VATE)
profile: Avram 'Avie' Glazer, son of the late shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer, has co-chaired Manchester United with his brother Joel since the family's 2005 takeover. The siblings sold a quarter of their stake to Jim Ratcliffe in 2023. The family has owned the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers since 1995, and he chairs holding company INNOVATE Corp. He also owns the Desert Vipers cricket club in Dubai.
interesting_fact: From 1995 to 2009 he was chairman and CEO of Zapata Corporation, the oil company founded by George H.W. Bush. He also previously ran Omega Protein and Safety Components International, giving him an energy-industry angle beyond sports.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Rochester, NY, he was named Junior Achievement's Outstanding Young Businessman of the Year in 1978. After law school he also studied at Peking University and Fudan University in Shanghai. With his wife Jill he founded Glazer Hall, a performing-arts centre in Palm Beach, in 2025.

public_contacts.value: ir@innovatecorp.com (INNOVATE Corp., where he is chairman)

notes: Glazer ownership is controversial among Man Utd fans, so avoid that in outreach; the energy (Zapata) or INNOVATE infrastructure angle is a better fit. INNOVATE sold DBM Global to IES Holdings in Oct 2026. The Manchester United IR site exposed no scrapeable email.

name: Liang Yanfeng
current_role: Chairman/leader of Zhonggeng Group (中庚集团), Fuzhou, per Forbes (profile last updated 2021)
profile: Forbes describes Liang Yanfeng (梁衍锋) as the self-made head of Fuzhou-based Zhonggeng Group, which has interests in real estate, industrial parks and financial investments. He dropped off the Forbes and Hurun lists after 2021-22, and I could not confirm his current status.
notes: Very little verifiable public information. The Forbes profile has not been updated since April 2021, the company domain zhonggeng.com shows 'site under construction', and Baidu Baike blocked access. The web-search budget was exhausted, so current status (and whether he dropped off the lists due to wealth loss) is unverified. Low priority.

name: Pier Luigi Piana
current_role: Minority shareholder (~8-10%) and longtime deputy chairman of Loro Piana (LVMH); current board title unverified
profile: Pier Luigi Loro Piana (b. 1951, Milan; Bocconi economics graduate) is the sixth-generation heir of the Loro Piana cashmere and wool house. With his late brother Sergio he took the brand global, then sold 80% to LVMH in 2013 for $2.6bn, keeping a minority stake. He is a well-known superyacht sailor and hosts the Loro Piana Superyacht Regatta.
interesting_fact: The Loro Piana family began trading wool in the early 1800s, and the company marked 200 years in 2012. The clothing firm itself was founded in 1924 by his grandfather Pietro.
deep_cut_fact: A sustainable-materials enthusiast, he built his sailing yacht My Song with linen fibre in place of glass fibre in bulkheads, floors and ceilings. He has said: 'Linen just uses sun and rain... To make a kilo of linen you use less CO2 than to make any other fibre.'
notes: The input name 'Pier Luigi Piana' refers to Pier Luigi Loro Piana. He is private, with no published personal or office channel found; the realistic route is Loro Piana / LVMH corporate communications. Sailing and sustainable materials are good hooks. Avoid mentioning his late brother or the loss of the yacht My Song in 2019.
